topic.subject: maths
topic.title: Order of operations (BODMAS)
topic.scope: BODMAS/PEMDAS precedence; multiplication before division is wrong, they have equal rank and go left to right; same for addition and subtraction; brackets order; 8-3+2 and 48÷2×3; negative signs with brackets; calculator versus hand results

nodes.name: Multiplication and division have equal rank
Addition and subtraction have equal rank
Multiplication/division come before addition/subtraction
external_prereqs: meaning of multiplication as repeated addition

nodes.name: Work equal-rank operations from left to right
A minus sign before a bracket changes every sign inside
A number touching a bracket multiplies the whole bracket
Fraction bar groups numerator and denominator
Do one operation per line, copy the rest
Scientific calculators apply BODMAS; basic ones may not
Brackets change the meaning of an expression

misconceptions.statement: Multiplication always comes before division because M comes before D in BODMAS.
misconceptions.why: The letters in the word BODMAS are read as a strict ranking.
misconceptions.fix: Multiplication and division have the same rank, so we do whichever comes first from the left.

misconceptions.statement: In 8 - 3 + 2, addition must be done before subtraction, so the answer is 3.
misconceptions.why: Student treats A before S in BODMAS as a strict order, ignoring that addition and subtraction have equal rank.
misconceptions.fix: Addition and subtraction have equal rank, so work left to right: 8 - 3 = 5, then 5 + 2 = 7.
misconceptions.root_belief: Letter order in BODMAS fixes the order of operations
misconceptions.source_hint: research on student errors with order of operations

misconceptions.statement: In 48 ÷ 2 × 3, multiplication is done first, so the answer is 8.
misconceptions.why: Student believes multiplication always outranks division, ignoring left-to-right rule for equal rank.
misconceptions.fix: Division and multiplication have equal rank, so go left to right: 48 ÷ 2 = 24, then 24 × 3 = 72.
misconceptions.root_belief: Multiplication outranks division in every expression
misconceptions.source_hint: studies of students' misuse of BODMAS/PEMDAS mnemonics

misconceptions.statement: In 2 × 3², you multiply 2 × 3 first and then square, so the answer is 36.
misconceptions.why: Student reads the expression left to right and ignores that orders (powers) rank above multiplication.
misconceptions.root_belief: Operations are always done in written left-to-right order
misconceptions.source_hint: research on exponent and order-of-operations errors

misconceptions.why: Student reads the index as a multiplier instead of the number of times the base is multiplied by itself.
misconceptions.fix: 3² means 3 × 3 = 9; the small number tells how many times the base is used as a factor.
misconceptions.root_belief: A power means base times the index

misconceptions.statement: In brackets inside brackets, you should start with the outermost bracket first.
misconceptions.why: Student works from the left or outside, as they read, rather than from the innermost bracket.
misconceptions.fix: Simplify the innermost bracket first and then move outward step by step.
misconceptions.root_belief: Work from outside in, following reading direction

misconceptions.statement: Curly brackets { } are always done before round brackets ( ) because they are bigger.
misconceptions.why: Student judges priority by the size or look of the bracket instead of by nesting.
misconceptions.fix: Round ( ) is cleared first, then { }, then [ ] when they are nested in that order; work from the innermost bracket outward.

misconceptions.statement: In 10 - (3 + 2), the minus sign only changes the first number inside, so it is 10 - 3 + 2 = 9.
misconceptions.why: Student drops the bracket and applies the minus sign only to the first term.
misconceptions.fix: The minus sign applies to the whole bracket: 10 - (3 + 2) = 10 - 5 = 5, or 10 - 3 - 2 = 5.
misconceptions.root_belief: A minus sign affects only the next term
misconceptions.source_hint: research on bracket expansion and sign errors

misconceptions.statement: In 4(3 + 2), the 4 touching the bracket means 4 is added to the numbers, giving 4 + 3 + 2 = 9.
misconceptions.why: Student ignores that a number written next to a bracket means multiplication.
misconceptions.fix: No sign between a number and a bracket means multiply: 4(3 + 2) = 4 × 5 = 20.

misconceptions.statement: In (6 + 4) ÷ 2, the fraction bar in 6 + 4 over 2 divides only the 4, so the answer is 8.
misconceptions.why: Student does not see the fraction bar as a bracket around the numerator, so divides only the nearest number.
misconceptions.fix: The bar groups the whole numerator: (6 + 4)/2 = 10 ÷ 2 = 5.

probe.question: Find the value of (6 + 4)/2 written as a fraction.

misconceptions.root_belief: A fraction bar divides only the adjacent number
misconceptions.source_hint: research on hidden grouping in fractions

misconceptions.statement: To save time, you can do all the operations in one line without copying the rest, and the answer will still be right.
misconceptions.why: Student combines several operations at once and loses or changes terms that were not yet worked.
misconceptions.fix: Do one operation per line and copy the remaining expression unchanged, so no term is dropped.

probe.question: Simplify 12 + 6 ÷ 3 - 1 step by step. What is the first line after one step?

misconceptions.root_belief: Skipping written steps never causes mistakes

misconceptions.statement: A basic calculator always gives the right answer for 2 + 3 × 4 because it follows BODMAS.
misconceptions.why: Student trusts every calculator, not knowing basic ones may evaluate in the order keys are pressed.
misconceptions.fix: Scientific calculators apply BODMAS and give 14; basic ones may work left to right and give 20, so check by hand.

probe.question: A basic calculator shows 20 for 2 + 3 × 4. Is it correct?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, the calculator is always correct, so 20

misconceptions.source_hint: research on calculator use and order of operations
